transcript: Let's talk about all of the performances at the 2026 Tonys. the good, the bad, and the confusing. Starting with the good, of course, we have to talk about this opening number. I think it is easily the best opening we have had since 2013 when Neil Patrick Harris did bigger. And in many ways kind of feels like a spiritual successor. Not just because they had Neil Patrick Harris make an appearance, but in the way it was able to incorporate and give love to all of the shows of the season. But it never really veered into corny slash cringe territory. And overall I thought that pink was a really excellent host. I also found the Rachel Zegler Chorus Line performance kind of strange. Not because she wasn't good, she sounded amazing. But it felt more like just a random performance rather than a tribute to a Chorus Line. Like, where was the chorus? Where was the line? On the flip side though, I did really love Leslie Odom Jr's in Memoriam. I thought it was beautifully sung and a perfect song for the segment. Back to the weird and random side of things. We have the Chicago performance, which I also found to be kind of odd. We start with Alex Newell. Makes sense. Tony winner did it on Broadway. But then we go into these random celebrity cameos which just felt so out of place. But underrated joke. I did like that they gave Dylan Mulvaney six. And then we go into pink singing all that jazz, which, again, just kind of random. She sounds great, but, like, the show's been running for 30 years on Broadway. You couldn't find someone that has done it on Broadway. The Book of Mormon performance, I thought was really fun, and it really does seem like the cast has not skipped a beat. I appreciate it that they were all in full costume. They did the full staging, in contrast to, like, the Hamilton and Spring Awakening performances, where they just kind of wore nice clothes and sang the songs. There's definitely an added layer seeing everything be recreated. As for the show performances, I thought they all were pretty good. Not personally what I would have chosen, but I thought most of them got across what they needed to get across. I like some of the creative intros we got this year, like schmigadoon and two strangers starting with their characters wandering into Radio City Music Hall. We also had, like, Rachel Dratch and Marla Mindelle introduce their shows in character. To be honest, I'll always prefer to random celebrity who is tangentially related to the show introducing it. The cats one I thought worked well because they were all producers on the show and clearly very passionate about the material. But, like, Adrian Brody introducing the ragtime performance, just bizarre. I was also kind of sad that there was no closing number. I feel like They've kind of fallen out of fashion in recent years, but I used to love when they would end the show with, like, a recap song of everything that happened in the ceremony. And without one, the ending always kind of feels anticlimactic.
